title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, TMTG treasury, Cumberland/Don Wilson
summary: Trump signed EO 14233 creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve on 2025-03-06, and the SEC dismissed its Cumberland DRW case with prejudice on 2025-03-27. TMTG announced a ~$2.5B bitcoin-treasury raise on 2025-05-27, which closed at ~$2.44B gross. DRW Investments (Don Wilson's firm) bought ~4M TMTG shares (~$100M) as part of it. The timing is loose ('around that time' is ~12 weeks), the investor was DRW rather than Wilson personally, and the dismissal was agreed in principle on 2025-02-20, before the TMTG deal was public. No quid pro quo is documented beyond the sequence of events.

sub_claims.statement: Trump signed an executive order creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.
sub_claims.finding: EO 14233 was signed 2025-03-06. It funds the reserve with forfeited government BTC that may not be sold; any further buying must be budget-neutral.

sub_claims.statement: Around that time TMTG announced a $2.5B raise to establish its own bitcoin reserve.
sub_claims.finding: TMTG announced the plan on 2025-05-27, about 12 weeks after the EO: ~$1.5B in stock plus $1B in convertible notes from ~50 institutions. It closed on 2025-05-30 at ~$2.44B gross (~$2.32B net).

sub_claims.statement: Don Wilson is one of the TMTG investors.
sub_claims.finding: Per FT-cited reports and SEC filings (June 2025), DRW Investments, founded and controlled by Wilson, bought nearly 4M TMTG shares worth ~$100M in the bitcoin-treasury financing. Jane Street (~$375M) was the largest buyer.

sub_claims.statement: Weeks earlier, the SEC enforcement case against Wilson's crypto firm Cumberland was dismissed with prejudice.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC sued Cumberland DRW in October 2024 (unregistered dealer, >$2B in crypto). Dismissal was agreed in principle on 2025-02-20 and announced on 2025-03-04. The joint stipulation to dismiss with prejudice was filed 2025-03-27 (LR-26276), with no admission and no penalty. That was ~8-9 weeks before the TMTG purchase.

sub_claims.statement: Cumberland denied any quid pro quo or connection between the TMTG investment and the SEC dismissal.
sub_claims.finding: The denial was given privately to Coffeezilla and cannot be independently checked. It is consistent with DRW's public statements that the stake was a strategic balance-sheet decision and that Wilson has long called for a clear regulatory framework.

corrections: Transcript says the TMTG raise came 'around that time' as the EO. The EO was signed 2025-03-06 and TMTG announced on 2025-05-27, about 12 weeks later.
Transcript says '$2.5 billion raised'. That was the announced size; the deal closed at ~$2.44B gross (~$2.32B net).
Transcript says Don Wilson invested. The documented buyer is DRW Investments, his firm; Cumberland is DRW's crypto unit.
The Cumberland dismissal was agreed in principle with SEC staff on 2025-02-20 and announced 2025-03-04, before TMTG's treasury plan was public.
denials_and_context: Cumberland/DRW deny any connection and say the TMTG stake was a bitcoin balance-sheet decision.
The SEC dropped the case as part of a broad retreat from Gensler-era crypto cases; Kraken, Consensys and Coinbase cases were dropped around the same time.
About 50 institutions took part in the raise; Jane Street's ~$375M was nearly four times DRW's stake.

TMTG is controlled by Donald J. Trump's revocable trust, so investing in it benefits the President's business; CREW raised 'policy-for-investment' concerns. No quid pro quo is documented, and the link is timing only.
